obtained.how: Internet Archive item, openly downloadable (not access-restricted, no borrow, no login): the scan of Transactions of the American Fisheries Society vol. 69 (Sixty-ninth annual meeting, June 26-27, 1939) in the Serials in Microfilm collection; the article (printed pp. 205-209 = scan PDF pp. 207-211) indexed with getsrc --file --pages 207-211; Tables 1 and 2 read on the page images

bibliography.checked_against: the article's title page in the volume scan and Crossref
bibliography.note: Edward C. Raney & Dwight A. Webster (Cornell University), 'The food and growth of the young of the common bullhead, Ameiurus nebulosus nebulosus (LeSueur), in Cayuga Lake, New York', Trans. Am. Fish. Soc. 69: 205-209. The volume is the proceedings of the 1939 meeting; Crossref dates the article 1940 (the DOI carries 1939), so '1940' with vol. 69 is consistent with Crossref.

claims.claim: first summer: crustaceans ~60 % (mostly ostracods and cladocerans), chironomid larvae ~25 %
claims.location: p. 205 (scan PDF p. 207), abstract; p. 206 (PDF p. 208), Results; Table 1, p. 207 (PDF p. 209)
claims.quote: The main staples were Crustacea (approximately 60 per cent) and Diptera
claims.conditions: 170 young-of-year examined, 21 June-10 October 1938, quiet weedy coves of lower Fall Creek and Cayuga Lake at Ithaca, NY (12.9-56.3 mm mean SL); percentages are estimated original volume of the whole alimentary-tract contents. Table 1 totals: Cladocera 25.0, Ostracoda 20.5, Copepoda 4.3, Isopoda 6.7, Amphipoda 2.4 (crustaceans 58.9 %), Diptera 24.3 %. 'Almost all of the Diptera taken were chironomid larvae while 80 per cent of the Crustacea were ostracods and cladocerans.'
claims.note: The table's '(full text not obtained)' tag can go: the full text is now read.

claims.claim: Cayuga Lake, NY, 1938: 57.5 mm on 30 September; 68 mm (41-93) on 10 October
claims.conditions: mean total length (mm) of preserved young-of-year (10 % formalin, then 70 % alcohol); n = 27 on 30 September (range 45-79 mm TL) and 53 on 10 October (range 41-93 mm TL); standard length means 47.7 and 56.3 mm
claims.note: Read on the page image. The table's '(relayed by a search summary of a species profile; unverified)' tag can be replaced by the direct citation. Note the lengths are of preserved fish.

notes: Other useful values: young bullheads fed mostly at dusk and night (day stomachs often empty); spawning mostly in the first three weeks of June at Ithaca; adults enter the coves at 50-55 °F (early April); mean TL 15.2 mm on 21 June, 42.0 mm on 5 August; 'the mean total length did not exceed 3 inches at the end of the first growing season, a few individuals reached a total length of 4 inches'. Fish (a cyprinid) and fish eggs were 1.3 % of the food. The 95-MB volume scan was deleted after indexing; the kept Raney_Webster_1940.pdf is the whole volume (getsrc kept only the article's text).
